record.paper: Colouring Graphs with Sparse Neighbourhoods: Bounds and Applications

dossier_meta.paper: Colouring Graphs with Sparse Neighbourhoods: Bounds and Applications
dossier_meta.statement_text: Let $G$ be a $\delta$-sparse graph. What is the largest $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(\delta)$ such that $\chi(G) \leq (1-\varepsilon)(\Delta+1)$?
dossier_meta.context_text: This isolates the second step in the King–Reed proof: given neighbourhood sparsity, bound the chromatic number below $\Delta+1$. Molloy–Reed obtained $\varepsilon(\delta)\approx 0.0238\delta$ and Bruhn–Joos improved to $\approx 0.1827\delta - 0.0778\delta^{3/2}$; the paper further improves this using an iterative naive colouring procedure.
